purpose: Explain why selected Lab products, standards, research testbeds, services, and prior systems exist as experimental environments; connect each to the methods it exercises, the proposition it tests, the evidence that could validate it, and the result that may transfer elsewhere.
coverageNote: Representative seed, not the full product catalog. The records below are drawn from current public product surfaces; historical work remains explicitly historical and research pilots remain unvalidated until their stated tests are run.

methods.label: Boundary analysis
methods.description: Make containment, interfaces, exclusions, obligations, and consequential crossings explicit.

methods.label: Representational mechanics
methods.description: Test what a representation preserves, exposes, distorts, or loses as perspective and resolution change.

methods.label: Provenance & governance
methods.description: Keep source, claim status, disagreement, review, promotion, supersession, and responsibility reconstructable.

methods.label: Closure & repair
methods.description: Treat failure, contestability, correction, supersession, and downstream repair as part of the represented system.

methods.label: Consequence tracing
methods.description: Follow how a local transition changes downstream options, obligations, risks, or affected parties.

methods.label: Multi-resolution projection
methods.description: Move between local and larger contexts while preserving identity, path, provenance, and semantic continuity.

methods.label: Adaptive computation
methods.description: Allocate computational attention according to measured structure, change, defect, or consequence rather than uniform geometry alone.

methods.label: Public legibility
methods.description: Join operational context into a representation that people outside the originating system can inspect and act from.

experiments.label: Corpus Forge
experiments.posture: specified lifecycle + validation targets; production performance not established
experiments.testEnvironment: A heterogeneous research corpus with sources, claims, evidence, contradictions, review decisions, maturity changes, and supersession history.
experiments.whySelected: Knowledge work is a severe representation problem: compression is useful, but consequential claims become unsafe when source, status, disagreement, and replacement history disappear.
experiments.proposition: A corpus can behave as a governed memory system in which consequential claims remain reconstructable, challengeable, promotable, supersedable, and repairable.
validation: reconstruct a public claim back to material sources and review decisions
detect contradictory evidence that remains unresolved
prevent lower-maturity notes from silently appearing as established claims
identify downstream objects affected by a repaired or withdrawn claim
failureSignals: promotion loses provenance or material disagreement
supersession erases why an earlier representation existed
repair cannot identify affected downstream objects
review burden makes the proposed operating model impractical at useful scale
experiments.claimBoundary: Corpus Forge is an active research-operations method and software program, not a proven production-ready knowledge-management platform and not a claim that provenance eliminates hallucination, disagreement, stale knowledge, or review error.

experiments.label: Boundary First UX
experiments.posture: semantic standard + reference demonstrations; conformance levels remain proposed
experiments.testEnvironment: Complex interfaces that must change perspective, scale, context, and renderer without silently changing the represented world's meaning.
experiments.whySelected: Interfaces are where representation becomes action. UX therefore provides a direct environment for testing whether boundaries, provenance, consequence, and repair can remain visible while local views stay usable.
experiments.proposition: A semantic interaction grammar can let users move among bounded representations while preserving identity, provenance, consequence, path, and scoped closure across renderer changes.
validation: represented containment boundary remains explicit
identity and provenance survive transformations
transitions have declared semantics
consequences can be traced
accessible routes remain semantically complete
closure is scoped and earned
failureSignals: visual metaphor has no operational semantics
zoom or reframe changes meaning without declaring the transformation
accessible representation loses essential semantic state
local simplicity erases the larger context required for consequence
experiments.claimBoundary: Boundary First UX is a working semantic interaction standard, not a mandatory visual skin, component library, or established proof that existing design systems are obsolete.

experiments.label: Boundary-First Chess
experiments.posture: complete manuscript draft + teaching grammar; comparative performance not established
experiments.testEnvironment: A fully rule-bounded adversarial state space with observable positions, legal transitions, forcing constraints, immediate feedback, established analysis, and strong external benchmarks.
experiments.whySelected: Chess makes constrained possibility unusually visible: the rules are complete, state is inspectable, consequences arrive quickly, and Boundary First language can be checked against established tactical, positional, and engine analysis.
experiments.proposition: Reading boundary, reachability, pressure, continuation, defect, and repair before deep calculation can provide a useful explanatory grammar for why candidate moves succeed or fail.
validation: candidate-move quality before deep calculation
recognition of overloaded defenders and hidden obligations
ability to explain how a move changes reachable state space
transfer from tactical examples to positional continuation and conversion
agreement with established chess analysis on the actual position
failureSignals: the vocabulary merely renames existing concepts without improving explanation or discrimination
boundary-first reading conflicts with concrete rules or strong chess analysis
illustrative teaching patterns fail to generalize beyond hand-picked examples
transferTargets: explanations of local action under adversarial constraint
experiments.claimBoundary: The doctrine does not claim improved rating, tournament performance, or superiority to established coaching systems without comparative evidence; illustrative patterns are not engine or empirical validation.

experiments.label: Boundary First Weather
experiments.posture: explicit hypothesis + validation ladder; forecast or efficiency improvement not established
experiments.testEnvironment: Weather-like PDE simulation where evolving boundaries, fluxes, model disagreement, forecast error, adaptive refinement, and computational cost can be measured against matched baselines.
experiments.whySelected: Weather contains multiscale transport and nonuniform change under high computational cost, making it a demanding domain for testing whether explicit boundary and defect information can guide where additional attention is valuable.
experiments.proposition: Forecast-relevant novelty, error, and cross-scale information may concentrate disproportionately around evolving lower-dimensional structures enough to support useful boundary-aware diagnostics or selective computation.
validation: compare boundary-selective refinement with matched uniform-refinement baselines
measure wall-clock time and update count
measure forecast-relevant, boundary-position, transport, and conservation error
test transition-detection lead time and compute spent outside active regions
advance only through an explicit validation ladder from toy systems toward established-model comparison
failureSignals: boundary indicators do not predict where consequential model disagreement or error concentrates
selective refinement costs more without preserving declared structure
conservation or numerical defects erase any computational advantage
performance appears only in toy cases and fails matched higher-fidelity comparison
experiments.claimBoundary: Boundary First Weather does not currently claim better forecasts, faster operational NWP, earlier severe-storm prediction, replacement of existing models, or external institutional validation.

experiments.label: Agency + Representation Audit
experiments.posture: bounded professional diagnostic; not certification or delegated institutional authority
experiments.testEnvironment: One consequential institutional or software process with identifiable authority, representations, transitions, affected parties, contest paths, and repair obligations.
experiments.whySelected: Consequential systems often distribute authority across policy, people, software, vendors, models, and interfaces while concentrating consequence elsewhere; a bounded audit makes the whole chain available for reconstruction.
experiments.proposition: A consequential process can be made more inspectable by reconstructing authority → representation → consequence → contestability → repair as one bounded operating relationship.
validation: material findings trace to observed artifacts, declared rules, executable behavior, stakeholder accounts, or labeled inference
authority and representation maps can be reconstructed
affected parties and downstream consequences can be identified inside scope
contest and correction paths can be exercised or shown missing
repair ownership gaps become explicit enough to prioritize
failureSignals: the process cannot be bounded tightly enough to reconstruct
the audit maps a decision but not downstream consequence or correction
inference is promoted beyond available evidence
findings imply institution-wide conclusions from one bounded process
experiments.claimBoundary: The audit is a systems diagnostic. It does not provide legal advice, regulatory certification, algorithmic fairness or safety certification, cybersecurity certification, or a universal verdict on the institution.

experiments.label: CityWatch
experiments.posture: prior civic delivery and standing; not a current municipal relationship and not retroactive validation of later Boundary First doctrine
experiments.testEnvironment: A municipal transparency system joining project, spending, infrastructure status, timeline, media, and geographic context into a citizen-facing representation.
experiments.whySelected: CityWatch is useful as prior executable evidence that disparate civic records can be reconciled into a public representation. It is retained as lineage and standing, not rewritten as a controlled Boundary First experiment that did not exist under that name at the time.
experiments.proposition: Integrated public representation can make a civic system's operational and financial context more legible than isolated records alone.
validation: historical implementation was delivered
multiple operational and civic record types were joined in one citizen-facing representation
requirements and delivery experience are retained as prior work
failureSignals: later Boundary First concepts are projected backward as if they governed the original implementation
historical outcomes or awards are asserted without retained or independently recoverable evidence
the historical relationship is presented as a current Augusta-Richmond County affiliation
experiments.claimBoundary: CityWatch supports claims about historical implementation and delivery experience. Current municipal sponsorship, endorsement, later outcome claims, and unverified awards remain outside that boundary.
